testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a car pulls out in front of you and you cannot stop, what should you do?

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it is their fault.
Swerve to avoid the other car.
Put your vehicle in reverse.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve to avoid the other car.
questions.explanation: If another car pulls in front of you, try to brake if you have room to stop safely. If you do not have room to stop, swerving may be safer.

questions.question: What can affect how far your vehicle travels before it stops?

options.text: Speed.
Engine oil.
Time of day.
Traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: When should you watch for black ice?

options.text: When it is snowing.
When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and snow is on the ground.
Just after a rainstorm.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safety of loaded cargo?

options.text: Only the driver can load cargo.
The person who loads the cargo is responsible for its safety.
Someone else can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
Only a shipping company employee can load cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone else can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
questions.explanation: No matter who loads the cargo, the driver is always responsible for keeping it safe.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges help a driver:

options.text: Are often misleading.
The only way to know if something is wrong with the vehicle.
Find out if something is wrong with the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find out if something is wrong with the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for any problems.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Listen for unusual noises.
Speed up the engine.
Turn up the radio.
Turn on the heater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, listen for any strange noises that might mean something is wrong.

questions.question: What is the horn used for?

options.text: To show that you are angry.
To alert other drivers that you are nearby.
To frighten other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: To alert other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others that you are there. Be careful with the horn because it can startle other drivers. Only use it when needed.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Should never be used.
Protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
questions.explanation: Header boards, called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?

options.text: Water.
Cardboard.
Brake fluid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Why should you be careful around a stopped bus?

options.text: There is no concern since the bus is stopped.
Only if passengers are getting off the bus.
You should always be careful, even if you do not see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always be careful, even if you do not see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby, and the bus might block your view of them or their view of you.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes fail on a long downhill?

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then on again to reset the brakes.
Pump the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill, use an escape ramp if available. If no escape ramp exists, look for other ways to stop, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Challenge them.
Ignore their gestures.
Avoid making eye contact.
Try to get out of their way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Challenge them.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not provoke them by making eye contact, racing, or refusing to move. Ignore any gestures meant to provoke you.

questions.question: The liver can process about ____ per hour.

options.text: One alcoholic drink
Two alcoholic drinks
Three alcoholic drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink
questions.explanation: Drinking faster increases your blood alcohol content (BAC). The liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing, with frequent blinking
Yawning repeatedly or rubbing your eyes
Staying in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, missing exits, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless. Staying in your lane is normal driving behavior.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually do not freeze.
Usually have no moisture, so they cannot freeze.
Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
Should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler. They can remain icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: Escape ramps are used to:

options.text: Only for cars, not trucks.
Leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhills to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, leakage should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.

options.text: 1 psi
2 psi
3 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test, air brake leakage must not exceed 2 psi per minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: During an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Swerve your trailer right and stop.
Stop in a straight line.
Swerve your trailer left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a straight line while maintaining control. This lets you turn if needed.

questions.question: If you drive through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Gently apply the brakes.
Stop in the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Avoid large puddles or moving water. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to low gear, and gently apply brakes. This keeps water out of the brake system.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking?

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate that cannot be speeded up. Cold showers, exercise, and coffee do not help. The only way to sober up is to wait.

questions.question: How far does an air brake-equipped vehicle need to stop when traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions?

options.text: 300 feet
100 feet
450 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should:

options.text: Accelerate.
Switch into a high gear.
Sound your horn.
Switch into a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Switch into a low gear.
questions.explanation: Switch into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go down.

questions.question: If you are not familiar with an area where you need to back up, you should:

options.text: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to see the area.
Not use both side mirrors because it can be distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can see how they do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to see the area.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and look at your path. Check what is on the sides and above to make sure you have enough space.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of deadly crashes.
Can be a good way to get somewhere quickly.
Should only be done on dry roads.
Is okay when traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of deadly crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many deadly crashes. Never drive faster than the speed limit and slow down for road conditions.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is:

options.text: 5 mph below your safe speed.
10 mph below your safe speed.
15 mph below your safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: When going downhill, hold the brake pedal until you reach a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release it. Repeat this process.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Are illegal in most states.
Help drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved, convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes brakes work without squeaking.
Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
Lubricates brake parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming in the system.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Load must be balanced properly. Too much weight on an axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight on an axle causes poor grip and handling problems.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Release air from the tanks.
Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early.
Signal the whole time you are turning.
Turn off your signal when your turn or lane change is done.
Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Start signaling well ahead of time and keep the signal on during the turn. If it does not turn off by itself, turn it off after you finish turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: When taking a driving test, what vehicle should you use?

options.text: You must use the same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
You can use any vehicle, even if it is not the type you will drive with your CDL.
The testing station will provide a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the same type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing this vehicle.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Open the radiator cap quickly.
Do not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to release pressure.

questions.question: When going down a long hill, how should you brake?

options.text: Use only the brakes.
Use mostly brakes and downshift occasionally.
Downshift first, then use brakes.
Never use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use brakes.
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use your engine's braking power to control your speed. Use your brakes only for extra slowing or stopping if needed.

questions.question: What is required for oversized loads?

options.text: Oversized loads can never be transported by truck.
Oversized loads should only be transported during the day.
Oversized loads must have proper authorization to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oversized loads must have proper authorization to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are oversized, over-length, or overweight.

questions.question: When parking with an offset back/left maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, pull forward first, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
questions.explanation: Stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and report the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Create your own route to show off your driving skills.
Follow the directions the examiner gives you.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.
Drive in an unsafe manner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions the examiner gives you.
questions.explanation: You must listen to and follow the examiner's directions during the on-road test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: What must be done with cargo inside a trailer?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It must be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured so it does not shift during transport.

questions.question: How should you use your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Only use them if there is traffic.
Check them regularly.
Check them regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of a road in winter?

options.text: They usually do not freeze.
They are blocked from moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay icy and slick even after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay icy and slick even after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They remain icy and slippery after ice has melted on other areas of the road.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ makes steering difficult.

options.text: 10 degrees
25 degrees
50 degrees

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
Not worry about how weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance your cargo carefully. Too much weight on one axle can damage it and make steering hard. Too little weight on an axle reduces traction and causes poor handling.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and blocking other drivers, you should:

options.text: Drive in the left lane.
Use your four-way flashers.
Drive without using any lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you. Check local laws to make sure flashers are permitted.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?

options.text: Single air brakes
Dual air brakes
Triple air brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brakes
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Do them the same way every time.
Check different items each time.
It is okay to check items in a different order each time.
You do not need to inspect every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something important.

questions.question: What is a drawback of retarders?

options.text: They are not allowed everywhere.
They help slow a vehicle.
They cannot be turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not allowed everywhere.
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders are noisy and are not permitted in all areas.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Use the parking brake.
Use the parking brake only on slopes.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When asked to change lanes on the driving test, check traffic carefully and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Without oil in its engine, a vehicle:

options.text: Will likely run smoothly.
Will make quick jerks while driving.
May have its engine damaged quickly.
Will get better gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have its engine damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine can be destroyed quickly without oil. Do not drive if your oil pressure gauge is low or moving up and down.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system has very low pressure:

options.text: No brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, low pressure in one system means either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop safely and have the air system repaired.
